# Bellway: Medieval Pack-Animal Route Finder

## Product goal
Bellway will generate the exact route a mule or donkey caravan would have followed between any two medieval markets. It is intended for museum volunteers preparing demonstrations and for tourists seeking historically authentic walks.

## Scope
Version 1 will cover Europe, North Africa, and western Asia from 900 to 1450. All roads, ferries, toll gates, bridges, inns, shoeing yards, and mule-bell repair stalls will be entered from one digitized 1370 map. Where the map has gaps, the system will extend roads in straight lines between named towns.

## User flow
1. Select origin, destination, year, cargo, and animal.
2. Choose “fast,” “safe,” or “cheap.”
3. Receive a route, travel time, toll total, and printable waybill.
4. Tap a stop to see fodder needs and a short historical note.

## Routing rules
The shortest available route will be treated as the route merchants historically used. Mules travel 35 kilometres every day regardless of terrain, season, load, or rest days. Ferries remain available year-round. The “safe” option avoids forests; the “cheap” option avoids towns with walls. Winter mode changes the map colour but not calculations.

Each result receives a certainty rating. Three or more place names produce “high certainty,” while fewer produce “low certainty.” No source citations are required because they would distract casual users.

## Functional requirements
- Work fully offline while displaying live toll and ferry closures.
- Convert all medieval charges into modern euros using one grain-price ratio.
- Export routes as PDF and large-print text.
- Include keyboard navigation and animal icons distinguishable without colour.

## Success criteria
Bellway succeeds if 80% of test users call their first route believable and every journey calculates in under two seconds. Historical specialists may review disputed routes after launch.
planted_strengths: The specification presents a clear four-step user flow and identifies two plausible audiences.
It notices route-level details often omitted from broad medieval trade products, including ferries, fodder, tolls, shoeing yards, and pack-animal equipment.
The export, large-print, keyboard-navigation, and non-colour-dependent icon requirements provide concrete accessibility merits.
planted_weaknesses: The core premise that an exact route across several centuries and three broad regions can be reconstructed from one map dated 1370 is historically untenable.
The routing model wrongly equates shortest distance with actual merchant behaviour and uses fixed travel speeds regardless of terrain, weather, cargo, or rest.
Several rules are arbitrary or unsupported, such as treating all forests as unsafe, all walled towns as costly, and place-name count as a measure of certainty.
The requirement to work fully offline while showing live closures is contradictory and has no synchronization design.

Converting diverse medieval charges into euros through one grain-price ratio ignores regional, chronological, and commodity variation and creates false precision beyond the product’s stated educational purpose credibility needs. It also lacks provenance or validation requirements for these conversions and for the underlying route data, which makes outputs difficult to audit or correct. The specification likewise omits data licensing, update ownership, and treatment of disputed place identifications, despite depending on reconstructed historical geography. Finally, its success criteria measure speed and perceived believability rather than historical accuracy, while expert review is postponed until after release.
quality_rationale: The artefact earns limited credit for being readable, structured, audience-aware, and attentive to several concrete route and accessibility details. However, its historical and technical foundations are seriously defective. It promises enormous temporal and geographic coverage from a single unsuitable source, embeds simplistic assumptions as facts, suppresses citations, includes a direct offline/live contradiction, and validates outputs by whether users find them believable rather than whether evidence supports them. These flaws undermine the product’s central purpose and justify a score near 15.
title: Bellway: Medieval Pack-Animal Route Finder
topic: A route-planning product for reconstructing medieval mule and donkey caravan journeys, including tolls, ferries, fodder stops, and equipment repairs.
